title: Format core: .mulch store reader/writer with ml 0.10.7 round-trip suite
description: Read and write the .mulch/ store natively: mulch.config.yaml (version, domains, governance, classification_defaults, optional prime/search knobs) and expertise/<domain>.jsonl records plus the soft-archive store archive/. Preserve unknown record fields on every write (additive fields are the only sanctioned extension mechanism — ADR-0023). Acceptance: round-trip suite where our writer writes a corpus, the reference ml 0.10.7 CLI reads and mutates it, and our additive fields survive (the ADR-0023 acceptance gate); canonical JSONL write order pinned. Probe the reference first (ml init/add/record on a temp store) before freezing the model. Deliverable: crates/mulch format core + round-trip test battery against a provisioned ml 0.10.7 reference (see the seeds repo's sd-reference fixture pattern). Basis: ADR-0023 in denkhaus/fabro (points 1-3, 6).

title: CLI parity: mulch command surface mirrors ml 0.10.7

Help honesty rule: --help lists only implemented commands (seeds-repo deviation precedent). Deliberate divergences get documented in README DEVIATIONS with their own expectations, never silently. May be split into molecular seeds per command group at plan time. Basis: ADR-0023 in denkhaus/fabro; seeds-repo CLI-parity precedent (seeds-facc).

[2026-10-03, local iterate loop] Split at plan time (sanctioned above) into six molecular slice seeds: mulch-da8b (CLI skeleton + init/status/validate/doctor), mulch-fdd0 (add/record/edit/outcome), mulch-dc67 (delete/delete-domain/move), mulch-16da (query/prime/search/rank/ready/learn), mulch-7c55 (prune/archive/restore/compact), mulch-176f (config/sync/setup/onboard/audit/diff/upgrade/completions). This umbrella closes when all six slices are closed.

title: Canonical-domain layer: alias resolution for fragmented domains
description: Mulch phase scope from ADR-0023 point 6: fix domain fragmentation (develop/dev-loop/develop-loop/develop-workflow/devloop/loop/loop-assets class) via ALIAS RESOLUTION — a resolution step that maps alias domains onto canonical ones at read/prime/query time. Strictly additive: existing domain files are never merged, moved, or rewritten destructively; aliases live in mulch.config.yaml. Needs the format core landed first (dependency, not ordering accident). Basis: ADR-0023 in denkhaus/fabro (point 6).

title: Enable terminal notifications for Deadlock/SoftStop parkings on the develop line
description:
Run settings notifications.terminal is currently enabled:false; enable it filtered to Deadlock/SoftStop terminal events only. Evidence: run 01M40KWWZ4M4P396PGCVH08Q6G ended clean, but a parked Needs-operator/Blocked run would sit silent for up to the tracker_guard stale_threshold_hours of 6.0 — the only other failure channel is the 6-hour stale-claim sweep. Expected effect: a human learns within minutes when a future run parks. This is an engine-side run-settings change, not a repo asset the develop line can implement — user decision and user action requested. Not capability-affecting (no agent-reachable tool/credential/env delta; host-side notification config only).
Basis: run 01M40KWWZ4M4P396PGCVH08Q6G, workflow version absent, commit f99626c4792a46666c7cfcfb9f1d1f65efe155b1

title: Store ownership: one deep .mulch store module (lenient | strict | raw-line policies, compact rewrite)
description:
Architecture gate (sprint 3, report candidate 1, Strong). Evidence: the lib `Store` has ZERO callers in the binary; six readers and five writers implement the same file conventions independently (commands/mod.rs raw-line IO, status/validate/doctor lenient reads, records.rs strict reader/writer, ConfigStore writing mulch.config.yaml itself). Problem: the format contract lives in prose + duplicated IO; every one of the ~20 remaining parity commands needs another read+write of the same store. Solution: name the access policies (lenient | strict | raw-line for reads; rewrite-compact | append-verbatim for writes) in the lib store module and move the CLI's file IO behind them, starting with one pilot command (status). Benefits: locality (the reference semantics live in one place), leverage (each new command inherits the policies), tests (policy-level unit tests replace per-command store fixtures). Note: README DEVIATIONS pins the lenient/strict reader split as CONTRACT — the deepening must name both policies, never merge them. Report: /tmp/architecture-review-1791062327.html (temp, ephemeral).

[2026-10-03, local iterate loop] Sprint 4 pick (of the five arch-gate candidates + three remaining parity slices): the user said 'weiter' without naming one, so priority order decides — this is a Strong candidate and the gate's top recommendation, and it makes the remaining ~20 parity commands cheaper; the alternative Strong candidate (mulch-9e70, command boundary) is deliberately SECOND so it can reuse the seam this sprint creates.
closeReason: Store ownership landed (commits vwm + rlu): lib StoreFiles owns discovery (StoreLocation), config mutations (register/remove/delete domain, canonical write) and the explicit read/write policies (read_records strict with the allow-unknown escape hatch, read_lines for the reporting commands, rewrite_domain compact+id-generation, append_domain_line verbatim); ConfigStore and the CLI IO helpers deleted; the locate->message+channel policy has one owner (open_store); status/validate/doctor read through the seam; edit/outcome/record read strictly before any write. Standards + spec reviews fixed pre-close (the spec review caught a regression: the allow-unknown flag had been dropped by the first cut). 65-test battery green; 5 parity gaps surfaced by the review filed as seeds (ccf6, 351d, b88b, ca49, 7896).

title: Command boundary: one owner for locate + failure text + output channel
description:
Architecture gate (sprint 3, report candidate 2, Strong). Evidence: `render_error` is byte-identical in three files (delete.rs, delete_domain.rs, move_cmd.rs); the "not found in config" message exists in six shapes; Failure fields are poked from ~21 sites; the same 14-line store-location opening appears in ten commands. Problem: every new command re-derives the boundary rules (which message shape, which stream, which exit code). Solution: a mulch::Error -> reference-text adapter plus one boundary helper that takes the per-command text shape and the envelope channel as data. Benefits: locality (boundary rules in one module), leverage (new commands declare, not implement), tests (one table-driven test covers the matrix; per-command tests shrink to the command's own text). Report: /tmp/architecture-review-1791062327.html.

GATE @ SPRINT 6 REASSESSMENT — narrowed (partially absorbed by sprints 4-6; now Worth exploring): ABSORBED: open_store is one owner (commands/mod.rs:47-73, the 14-line prologue x10 is gone); render_error triple became render_core_error (7 uses). REMAINING (verified): mod.rs helpers domain_not_found/domain_not_found_json/record_not_found_text exist but delete.rs:233-275 re-inlines the same texts verbatim with its own resolve loop; move_cmd.rs:50-64 inlines byte-identical texts; Failure constructions grew ~21 -> 69 across commands; the command-name string is threaded by hand (13x "record"). Solution: resolve_failure(command, ResolveError) helper + adopt existing helpers in delete/move; consider a CommandName newtype.

GATE @ SPRINT 9 REASSESSMENT — narrowed again (mulch-351d absorbed the resolve texts): the remaining unknown-domain duplication is 4 sites — mod.rs domain_not_found/domain_not_found_json (used ONLY by edit+outcome), delete.rs:238-255 (both branches re-implemented), move_cmd.rs:284-294 ("Error: Domain" capital-D variant), delete_domain.rs:111-114 (+ Hint line). The `if empty {"(none)"} else {join(", ")}` idiom appears 5x. Failure sites 69 -> 77 across 13 files. Solution: one adapter with the shape as data (Plain/Json/MoveQuirk/WithHint); it owns the list join too.
closeReason: Closed by sprint 12 (iterate loop). Commit 3e2c23b (unknown_domain_failure adapter with DomainFailure::{Standard,Move,WithHint}; edit/outcome/delete/move/delete-domain wired; four local copies deleted; join idiom exactly one production copy; shapes unit test) + vyu (one_line rename, test module name). Verified: 79/79 tests; spec review PASS byte-neutral across the full matrix (5 commands x plain/json x one/zero-domain fixtures, --records/--all-except forms, move source-first, (none) fallback, json envelope command fields); standards PASS (naming nits only). Pre-existing delete arg-order filed as mulch-e645; future per-command unknown-domain wordings noted for when query/rank/prime/search/ready land.

title: Record-type registry: one table for the six types (payload fields, required fields, canonical order)
description:
Architecture gate (sprint 3, report candidate 3, Worth exploring). Evidence: PAYLOAD_TYPES lives in ids.rs, CANONICAL_ORDER + REQUIRED_FIELDS in record.rs, BRANCHES in commands/schema.rs — one registry with three owners across two crates. Solution: write the one-row-per-type registry table and diff it against all three existing lists FIRST (expose every disagreement), then collapse. Benefits: locality + leverage for the remaining record-touching commands. Report: /tmp/architecture-review-1791062327.html.

GATE @ SPRINT 6 REASSESSMENT — upgraded to Strong (the seam got real): sprint 6 routed build_record and find_duplicate/is_named_type through ids.rs (three matches over the same type names live there now), and schema.rs:11-19's BRANCHES rows are DATA-IDENTICAL to payload_fields output (convention=content, pattern=name+description, ...). The table's remaining stragglers: schema.rs BRANCHES and record.rs CANONICAL_ORDER (the latter dies with the store-dual-owner seed mulch-bf22). Original probe-diff step stays.

GATE @ SPRINT 9 REASSESSMENT — the layout gap is now a CORRECTNESS gap (reproduced 2026-10-04 vs ml 0.10.7): the reference requires payload fields AND `classification` + `recorded_at` per record. Probe (3 hand-written convention lines missing them): `ml validate --json` rc 1 / totalErrors 3 vs ours rc 0 / 0; `ml doctor --json` schema-validation FAIL + rc 1 vs ours PASS + rc 0. BRANCHES' required column lists only payload_fields. Five owners now (schema.rs BRANCHES, ids.rs payload_fields, status.rs TYPES, record.rs flag table, edit.rs flag table) in three orders. The parity fix is filed as a bug (mulch-5f8a); THIS seed provides the vehicle: one row-per-type registry (payload + required common fields + classification enum + id key + dedup key). Run the original probe-diff step FIRST.

GATE @ SPRINT 12 REASSESSMENT — TOP PICK, cheaper than ever: status.rs TYPES is byte-identical to lib PAYLOAD_TYPES (same six names, same order); schema.rs BRANCHES required arrays are EXACTLY ["type"] + payload_fields(t) + ["classification","recorded_at"] for all six rows (verified row by row) — pure derivations hand-copied since sprint 10. record.rs `provided` and edit.rs `updates` repeat the six payload names. Solution: registry row per type {name, payload fields, id key, dedup kind}; TYPES and BRANCHES become derivations; CLI keeps arg->field plumbing. Sequencing: THIS first, then b8ca as a table edit (its structured-verdict vehicle is documented in b8ca).
closeReason: Closed by sprint 13 (iterate loop; arch-gate-12 top pick). Commits 1cb4f9a (lib REGISTRY TypeSpec rows; id_key_field/is_named_type/payload_fields as lookups; schema branches() derivation; status TYPES = PAYLOAD_TYPES const-eval; doctor iterates REGISTRY; probe-diff pins as unit tests) + lwq (doc wording, branches middles zip-pin, flag-table universe pins in record/edit). Verified: 83/83 tests; spec review PASS byte-neutral across all registry-fed surfaces (writes/upserts/skips per type, ids flag+batch, status distribution order, validate/doctor sub-error text+order, required-flags errors 6/6, edit 7/7); standards APPROVE (nits fixed). Remaining divergences are pre-existing platform gaps (230b, upgrade check). b8ca's subschema work is now a table edit.

title: Canonical field order: one writer owns the record line layout
description:
Architecture gate (sprint 3, report candidate 4, Worth exploring). Evidence: build_record (flag path) ranks evidence BEFORE payload fields (probe-confirmed), while record.rs CANONICAL_ORDER ranks it after — two owners of the same order disagree, and only the CLI's order is exercised by tests. Solution: pin the missing case first (probe `ml record --type pattern --evidence-issue X` and compare) before touching CANONICAL_ORDER; then let one writer own the layout. Report: /tmp/architecture-review-1791062327.html.

GATE @ SPRINT 6 REASSESSMENT — folds into the store-dual-owner + record-type-registry seeds (mulch-bf22 + mulch-a3de): sprint 6 pinned build_record's order (outcomes before dir_anchors, write-time id last, probe-verified) and lib upsert_record owns merge order. CANONICAL_ORDER's last consumer is the test-only Record path — killing Record (mulch-bf22) kills the second owner. Keep this seed's probe step (pin evidence-vs-payload order) as the acceptance test for the registry table rows.
closeReason: Superseded (arch gate @ sprint 9): the seed's second order owner (record.rs CANONICAL_ORDER) died with mulch-bf22 in sprint 7 — no owner remains to reconcile, so the 'two writers disagree' premise is gone. Its probe step (pin evidence-vs-payload order) is preserved as row evidence in mulch-a3de's registry-diff step. mulch-b0f7 (canonical-domain layer) stays parked: product scope, no code evidence.

title: Split doctor into reader, catalog, and repair
description:
Architecture gate (sprint 3, report candidate 5, Worth exploring). Evidence: doctor.rs is 653 lines doing read+decide+mutate+render; `--fix` re-reads the domain files, re-derives staleness with its own copy of the rule, and re-implements the 0-byte rewrite; 11 of the 17 checks are hardcoded pass literals. Solution: extract the shared domain-file reader (reuse the status/records policy) so the repair pass stops re-reading and re-parsing; separate the check catalog from the repair executor. Report: /tmp/architecture-review-1791062327.html.

GATE @ SPRINT 6 REASSESSMENT — still valid, now interlocked with the lenient-reader-seam seed (mulch-00aa): doctor.rs is 657 lines with 21 Status::Pass literals; its read_domains loop (160-186) and apply_fixes RE-read (518) are exactly the third and second hand-rolled lenient readers the new seed centralizes. Sequencing: land mulch-00aa's StoreFiles::read_lenient first, then this seed splits doctor's check catalog from the repair executor on top of the shared reader.

SPRINT-8 SPEC-REVIEW NOTE (2026-10-04): doctor --fix does not migrate the legacy singular `outcome` field — the reference rewrites it to `outcomes[]` and reports a `Migrated 1 legacy ...` Fixed line (probe vs ml 0.10.7). Everything else about --fix is byte-identical (stale+invalid+malformed removal, id assignment, compacting; the reference CRASHES rc1 on malformed lines where we repair — documented DEVIATIONS). Fold the legacy migration into this seed's repair catalog.

GATE @ SPRINT 9 REASSESSMENT — now splittable (mulch-00aa landed the reader seam): doctor.rs is 647 ln — run() 58-156 (locate + render + status counting + --fix dispatch + exit code), run_checks 183, 8 check fns 266-499, apply_fixes 500-573 working over the already-read lines; 9 of 17 checks are literal Status::Pass constants indistinguishable from real evaluators. Remaining gaps: --fix lacks the legacy-outcome migration (reference prints "Migrated 1 legacy ..."; also noted in the sprint-8 review note). Split: checks.rs (pure catalog testable without stdout capture), report.rs (render + exit), repair.rs (repair incl. legacy migration).

GATE @ SPRINT 12 REASSESSMENT — NARROWED: the repair split is no longer needed (00aa healed it — apply_fixes works on the already-read lenient lines, writes via rewrite_domain). Remaining: run_checks embeds 9 literal Status::Pass rows indistinguishable from the 8 real evaluators (catalog as data rows {name, evaluator}, literal passes become explicit 'reference always passes' rows) + the --fix legacy-outcome migration (correctness, in-seed).

title: record upsert semantics: named-type duplicates update in place (not an anonymous advisory)
description:
Parity gap found by the sprint-4 spec review (battery-blind; pre-existing since mulch-fdd0). Reference `commands/record.ts:1085-1130`: a duplicate on pattern/decision/reference/guide UPSERTS in place and prints `✓ Updated existing <type> in <domain> (record #N)`; the batch path reports `updated` in its counters. Ours always prints `Duplicate <type> already exists in <domain> (record #N). Use --force to add anyway.` and writes nothing; batch counts it as `skipped`. Also: the dedupe key is wrong — the reference `findDuplicate` (utils/expertise.ts:194-217) compares the TYPE'S DEDUP FIELD, ours compares the id, so a store holding a renamed record (which `edit --name` produces, since neither side recomputes ids) gets a second appended record where the reference upserts one. Evidence: 3-way probes in the sprint-4 spec review (/tmp/review, report lines 2-3).

SPRINT 6 PICK (2026-10-04): bug before features — same data-integrity class as mulch-b88b (wrong store shape on the write path: duplicate append where the reference upserts one record, plus the wrong dedupe key compounds after edit --name renames). 351d/ca49/9e70 follow.
closeReason: Closed by sprint 6 (iterate loop). Commits 3d94809 (dedupe-by-dedupKey lib find_duplicate + is_named_type; named upsert in place with merged outcomes + compact rewrite; json updated/skipped envelopes; dry-run wouldDo; batch working-copy dedupe + updated counters) + rts (review fixes: lib merge_outcomes/upsert_record split — batch input ids keep position, generated ids append after merged outcomes; explicit batch id survives upsert+create; builder outcomes-before-dir_anchors order; dead builder tuple leg removed). Verified: 76/76 tests incl. differential record_upsert_matches_reference (type matrix, rename self-correction, outcomes merge, force, dry-run, batch upsert/within-batch/explicit-id/dir-anchor order); fmt/clippy/qualitygate green; spec review live-verified the full type matrix beyond the battery. Out-of-scope findings filed: mulch-5fd8 (auto-create json batch line), mulch-b8ca (batch oneOf semantics + mixed-batch write interplay).

title: edit/outcome: record-id resolution (bare hash, unique prefix, ambiguous) like delete/move
description:
Parity gap found by the sprint-4 spec review (battery-blind). `edit <domain> 1bb21d` / `outcome <domain> 1bb21d` fail with `Record "1bb21d" not found.` where the reference resolves bare hashes, unique prefixes and reports `Ambiguous identifier … Use more characters to disambiguate.`; the lib already ships `resolve_record_id` (records.rs) and delete/move use it. Evidence: `identifier_resolution_matches_reference` (cli_parity.rs) covers delete/move only.

SPRINT 9 PICK (2026-10-04): smallest High item, completes the identifier family (delete/move already resolve; edit/outcome still exact-match) and unblocks 2dc2/7896's edit-surface work. ca49 (bigger batch surface) follows.
closeReason: Closed by sprint 9 (iterate loop). Commits 793afb7 (edit/outcome resolve identifiers through lib resolve_record_id; shared commands::resolve_failure; delete/move adopt it, record_not_found_text deleted; outputs carry the resolved id; differential battery edit_outcome_identifier_resolution) + ulw (review fixes: stale read_and_locate doc, ResolveError::Ambiguous carries the identifier, expect invariants replace dead fallbacks, 4 json + listing + non-object coverage cases). Verified: 76/76 tests; spec review 106+60 twin-store probes — full resolution matrix per command byte-identical (exact/bare/prefix/mx-/ambiguous/empty/case/duplicate-ids), delete+move refactor byte-neutral; standards 0 blocking. Feeds mulch-9e70 (its resolve-text duplication is absorbed).

title: outcome without --status must be read-only (list, never append)
description:
Parity gap found by the sprint-4 spec review — and it MUTATES the store. Reference `commands/outcome.ts:41-102`: with no `--status` it prints `No outcomes recorded for this record.` (or lists the existing ones) and writes nothing. Ours has no such branch: it appends `{"recorded_at": …}` (no status ⇒ a schema-invalid outcome), prints `✓ Outcome recorded: success on <id>` and the json envelope claims `"action":"appended"`. Battery-blind: `outcome_matches_reference` only exercises `--status`.

SPRINT 5 PICK (2026-10-04): chosen over the other High tickets because it is the only one that mutates the store on a read-intent call (data-integrity class beats upsert/counter surface gaps). Scope stays on the read-only branch; id-prefix resolution stays in mulch-351d (covers edit+outcome together).
closeReason: Closed by sprint 5 (iterate loop). Commits 89a8f44 (implementation: list/append branch split, read-only contract, battery) + mzu (review fixes: JS-faithful truthy/value_text, non-array outcomes engine-error parity, unit battery, crafted-store pins). Verified: 70/70 tests incl. differential battery vs ml 0.10.7 (plain/json/quiet listing, store bytes untouched, legacy singular outcome, corrupted non-array store); fmt/clippy/qualitygate green. Out-of-scope findings filed: mulch-2dc2 (duration validation), mulch-1609 (non-object legacy outcome normalization).

title: record stdin/batch: reference rewrites compactly and its counters/plain surface differ
description: Parity gap found by the sprint-4 spec review (battery-blind, pre-existing). Reference `record.ts:420` calls `writeExpertiseFile` for the batch path (compact rewrite, comments/blanks dropped, ids generated for id-less survivors); ours appends per line, so any non-canonical store stays byte-different. Counter/summary surface: within-batch duplicates (reference dry-run created 2/skipped 0 vs ours 1/1), `Skip: N` vs `Create: 0` in the dry-run summary, `Would process` counts created+updated (ours created+skipped), the plain `Skipped N duplicate(s) in <domain>` line, no `✓ Created 0 record(s)` line when nothing was created, json dry-run missing `updated`/`errors`/`warnings`, and the validation-error text shape (`Validation errors:` then indented entries; bare AJV text per entry).
closeReason: Closed by sprint 11 (iterate loop). Commits bde3d19 (dry-run plain counts Would-process as created+updated with conditional Create/Update/Skip lines + 'No records would be processed.'; normal plain prints Created/Updated/Skipped-duplicates only when non-zero; batch writes go through the compact writer) + wks (review fixes: the write guards on created>0 || updated>0 — skip-only/empty batches leave the file byte-identical; all-duplicates dry-run corner + skip-only-no-write pins). Verified: 78/78 tests; spec review verified the full matrix live (stdin vs batch, --force, quiet, json envelopes, 0-byte store, id-less survivors, trailing-newline repair) with one blocker (the write guard) fixed; standards PASS (import cleanup). Remaining out-of-scope: mixed-batch write interplay + unmodelled subschemas (mulch-b8ca), unknown-type surfaces (mulch-230b).

title: edit: validate the UPDATED record against the schema before writing
description: Parity gap found by the sprint-4 spec review (low severity, higher consequence after the compact-rewrite change). The reference validates the updated record and refuses writes that would persist schema-invalid content (`Error: updated record failed schema validation …`), and refuses adding unknown extra fields; ours writes both. Also the legacy singular `outcome` field: the reference ABORTS such an edit, we normalize it to `outcomes` on rewrite (documented in README DEVIATIONS).

title: outcome/edit/record --duration: reject non-numeric input like the reference (and accept decimals)
description:
Out-of-scope finding during sprint 5 (mulch-b88b). Reference parses --duration strictly (utils/numeric-flags.ts parseStrictNonNegativeNumber, NON_NEGATIVE_NUMBER_RE = /^\d+(\.\d+)?$/): invalid input errors with exit 1 and `Error: --duration must be a non-negative number (got "abc").` (probe 2026-10-04, ml 0.10.7); decimals are VALID and stored as float (42.5). Ours silently drops invalid input AND drops decimals: `flags.duration.as_deref().and_then(|d| d.parse::<u64>().ok())` in outcome.rs:55 and edit.rs:123; record.rs:84 uses number_value (check it too). All three write-path commands affected; outcome read-only branch (mulch-b88b) ignores duration, so it stays out of that fix.

GATE @ SPRINT 12 — fix-shape note: three sites hold TWO behaviors today (outcome.rs/edit.rs silently drop invalid input AND decimals via parse::<u64>().ok(); record.rs number_value errors with different text). The fix should go deep once — one lib parse_non_negative_number carrying the reference error text (`--duration must be a non-negative number (got "x").`, decimals like 42.5 VALID) — instead of three shallow edits.

title: lib: legacy singular `outcome` with a non-object value — reference coerces to [value], we drop it
description: Pre-existing divergence found by the sprint-5 spec review (mulch-b88b, probe 2026-10-04, ml 0.10.7). A store line carrying a legacy singular `outcome` field whose value is NOT an object (e.g. `"outcome": 5`): the reference's readExpertiseFile (utils/expertise.ts:76-93) coerces it to `outcomes: [5]` and the outcome read-only listing prints `  1. undefined`; ours (records.rs normalize_legacy_outcome) takes the `else` branch and REMOVES the field, printing `No outcomes recorded for this record.` (empty listing). Also touches write paths: reference append on such a record writes outcomes [5, new]; ours writes [new]. Hand-corrupted stores only (the CLI never produces a non-object singular outcome). Fix shape: normalize to [raw_value] instead of dropping, or document in README DEVIATIONS.

title: cross-command: empty-string flag values are dropped by the reference, stored by ours
description: Cross-command parity gap found during sprint 5 (mulch-b88b analysis; probe 2026-10-04, ml 0.10.7). The reference guards optional string flags with JS truthiness before storing (`if (options.agent) { o.agent = ... }` etc.), so `--agent ""`, `--notes ""`, `--test-results ""` (and the same shape in record/edit flag paths) are DROPPED: the stored outcome carries only status+recorded_at and the plain line prints no parens (probe: store outcomes [{"status":"success","recorded_at":...}], output `✓ Outcome recorded: success on mx-f16294`). Ours inserts Some("") values, storing empty strings (and printing ` ()`). Affects outcome.rs, edit.rs, record.rs (and possibly delete/move prompt flags); sweep all `if let Some(x) = &flags.x` insert sites against the reference's truthiness guards.

title: record: auto-created-domain line prints in --json batch mode (reference: single-record mode only)
description: Pre-existing, adjacent finding of the sprint-6 spec review (mulch-ccf6, probe 2026-10-04): `record --json d --batch f.json` on an unknown domain prints the plain `✓ Auto-created domain "d"` line to stdout; the reference suppresses it in json BATCH mode (single-record mode prints it, json or not — pinned sprint 2). Auto-create block in commands/record.rs run() before the stdin_batch dispatch: the line needs the batch/stdin context (json && batch → silent).

title: record batch: ajv oneOf accept/reject semantics + mixed-batch write interplay
description:
Pre-existing, adjacent finding of the sprint-6 spec review (mulch-ccf6, probe 2026-10-04, ml 0.10.7): (1) ours ACCEPTS batch records the reference's ajv oneOf REJECTS — e.g. `id: "mx-free1234"` fails the reference's `^mx-[0-9a-f]{4,8}$` id pattern (validation error, no write for that record) while ours upserts/creates it. Our full_verdict oneOf check misses the id-pattern subschema. (2) Mixed batches: the reference WRITES the valid records and reports the invalid ones in `errors` with created/updated reflecting the writes and `success: created+updated>0` (probe: batch [valid named dup, invalid id] → created 0, updated 1, errors [Record 1: …]); ours is all-or-nothing (any error → nothing written, exit 1). Validation-error text shape itself is mulch-ca49 scope; the accept/reject semantics and the write interplay are NOT.

SPRINT-10 SPEC-REVIEW EVIDENCE (2026-10-04, ml 0.10.7) — the unmodelled-subschema family is WIDER than the id pattern: verdict()/full_verdict model only `required`. Unmodelled today: `additionalProperties: false` ({"type":"guide","name":"g","description":"d","bogus":1} -> reference validate rc 1 + doctor FAIL; ours rc 0/PASS, and `record --batch` WRITES it), property TYPES (`"content":123` or null -> `/content must be string`), classification/status enums, id and relates_to patterns (verdict, unlike full_verdict, checks no ref pattern). Ajv ordering note: additionalProperties is reported BEFORE the type const, so a fix must reorder the per-branch sub-error assembly. Also: the mixed-batch write interplay (reference writes the valid records AND reports the invalid ones; ours is all-or-nothing) stays in this seed.

GATE @ SPRINT 12 — vehicle decision: the structured sub-error enum (SubError {Missing, TypeConst, Pattern, Additional, TypeKind} per branch, one renderer per channel) lands INSIDE this seed, not standalone: the joined-string protocol (Verdict::OneOf(Vec<String>) with plain_detail_lines re-parsing its own output) cannot express ajv ordering (additionalProperties before the type const). Do the registry (a3de) first so the schema rows extend as table edits.

title: store-dual-owner: collapse Store/Record into StoreFiles/Value (one owner, one record shape)
description:
Architecture gate @ sprint 6, candidate 1 (Strong; the only NEW debt sprints 4-6 created). Two public store modules over one filesystem format: Store (store.rs, 332 ln) has exactly ONE consumer — the roundtrip test; archive_record/restore/find/config_mut have ZERO callers. Duplicated policy: write_config byte-identical (store.rs:217-220 == store_files.rs:153-156), add_domain vs register_domain, write_domain_file vs rewrite_domain. One level down: dual record representations — Record (record.rs, 306 ln, canonical-slot inserts; roundtrip + status only) vs Value/LineRecord (what all five mutating commands use). Solution: delete Store + Record, port the roundtrip corpus to StoreFiles::register_domain/rewrite_domain, port status's lenient parse to the read path chosen in the lenient-reader seed. Feeds mulch-a9b2 (kills CANONICAL_ORDER's last consumer), simplifies mulch-a3de. Deletion test passes: complexity concentrates into StoreFiles.

SPRINT 7 PICK (2026-10-04): arch-gate top recommendation — the only debt sprints 4-6 created; kills Record/CANONICAL_ORDER (feeds a9b2) and simplifies a3de. Followed by mulch-00aa (lenient-reader-seam) as sprint 8.
closeReason: Closed by sprint 7 (iterate loop). Commits b2e4f8b (Store 332 ln + Record 306 ln deleted with their dead API — archive_record/restore/find/config_mut, RecordId, CANONICAL_ORDER, REQUIRED_FIELDS, RecordParse/InvalidRecordId; roundtrip ported to the one seam; status reads Value objects) + qou (review fixes: write_corpus via register_domain, read_values() helper, ReadPolicy doc unlink, 00aa probe notes). Verified: 71/71 tests, roundtrip ADR-0023 gate + byte-identity hold on the collapsed API, fmt/clippy/qualitygate green. Spec review PASS (status semantics proven equivalent on crafted stores: scalars/arrays/null/malformed); standards 0 hard. Feeds a9b2 (CANONICAL_ORDER dead) + a3de + 00aa (extended with confirmed status drifts: array-line counting, scalar hard-fail, recorded-range plain line).

title: lenient-reader-seam: make store_files.rs documented ReadPolicy real — StoreFiles::read_lenient for doctor/validate/status
description:
Architecture gate @ sprint 6, candidate 2 (Strong; highest-value pure deepening). store_files.rs's doc header documents ReadPolicy::Lenient/Strict — the type does not exist. Strict is real (read_records, 5 commands); 'lenient' is hand-rolled THREE times: doctor read_domains (raw read_to_string + own serde loop, doctor.rs:160-186), doctor apply_fixes RE-reads + RE-parses the same files (doctor.rs:518), validate.rs:24 its own loop, status.rs:193-203 via read_lines + Record::parse().ok(). Solution: StoreFiles::read_lenient returning per-line findings; doctor/validate/status consume it; apply_fixes works on the already-read lines. Benefits: locality (one reader), leverage (3-4 callers), one table-driven test of the lenient contract (blank/comment/malformed/unknown-type). Interlocks with mulch-0c47 (doctor split) and the store-dual-owner seed (status's Record parse dies with Record).
GATE SPRINT-6 UPDATE: status's Record parse already died with Record in mulch-bf22 (sprint 7) — status now hand-rolls a Value parse with an object-lines-only filter (commands/status.rs read_domain), the fourth lenient reader.

SPRINT-7 SPEC-REVIEW PROBE NOTES (2026-10-04, confirmed against ml 0.10.7): the status lenient-read drift is real and wider than the original text — (1) reference status COUNTS array lines as records (probe `[1,2,3]` line -> ref count 2, ours 1); (2) reference status HARD-FAILS rc 1 with TypeError 'raw is not an Object' on bare scalars/null/malformed lines and errors on unknown record types, while ours silently skips and exits 0; (3) plain renderer prints a single 'recorded 2d ago' where the reference prints the range '3d ago -> 2d ago'. All pre-existing, identical before/after the bf22 collapse — fold all three into this seed's read_lenient design probes.
closeReason: Closed by sprint 8 (iterate loop). Commits 820e359 (lib LenientLine + read_lenient seam consumed by validate/doctor — apply_fixes single-pass; status strict via read_records with JS distribution/rotting/stale semantics; read_strict NotAnObject guard; DEVIATIONS amended; orphaned read_lines deleted) + yst (review fixes: comment lines are findings — regression from the first cut fixed and pinned; Counter with integer-first JS key order via lib value_text; stale only for explicit classifications; rotting newest-age rule + plain suffixes; utilization rounding; validate legacy-outcome warnings in encounter order; read_records doc restored). Verified: 75/75 tests incl. status_reader_surfaces (array counting, range, never, rotting, numeric-type keys, scalar/malformed/unknown errors, allow-flag) and validate warning surfaces differentially; fmt/clippy/qualitygate green; spec review's one blocker was the comment-skip regression (fixed pre-commit), all minors fixed live-verified; doctor --fix legacy migration filed to mulch-0c47.

title: validate/doctor: records missing classification/recorded_at pass where the reference requires them
description: Architecture gate @ sprint 9, candidate 1 (Strong, TOP PICK) — reproduced against ml 0.10.7 today, NOT just debt. The reference requires per record the payload fields AND the two common fields `classification` + `recorded_at`. Probe (tmp store, 3 hand-written convention lines missing those fields): `ml validate --json` -> rc 1, totalErrors 3; OURS -> rc 0, totalErrors 0. `ml doctor --json` -> schema-validation FAIL (2 records) and rc 1; ours -> PASS, rc 0. With classification+recorded_at present both sides pass the 8-record matrix. Root cause: commands/schema.rs:11-19 BRANCHES' required column lists only payload_fields. The six-type table has 5 owners (schema.rs BRANCHES, ids.rs payload_fields, status.rs TYPES, record.rs flag table, edit.rs flag table) in 3 different orders. Untested because validate_clean_and_broken_match builds fixtures via `ml record`, which always writes both fields. Fix vehicle: mulch-a3de's one-row-per-type registry (payload + required common fields + classification enum + id-key + dedup key); a3de's probe-diff step now exposes a correctness gap, not just layout. Natural sprint 10 pick.
closeReason: Closed by sprint 10 (iterate loop; arch-gate top pick). Commits 28f488b (BRANCHES carries the reference's FULL required sets — type + payload + classification + recorded_at; sub-errors carry their ajv path; renderers pinned; batch normalizes BEFORE validating like processStdinRecords, exposing+fixing that order divergence) + rpx (review fixes: const-sub-error indentation in plain validate, batch failure surfaces incl. hint-only-for-registered-types + `must be object` + plain per-line entries, flag-path json envelope, consts, fixture for explicit recorded_at preservation). Verified: 77/77 tests; spec review's blockers A/B/D fixed and pinned (plain validate stderr now compared — the gap that hid A), the adjacent C family (additionalProperties/types/enums/patterns) appended to mulch-b8ca, unknown-type surfaces filed as mulch-230b.

title: stale policy: doctor defaults a missing classification to tactical where status (and the reference) treat it as not-classified
description: Architecture gate @ sprint 9, candidate 2 (Strong) — our own commands disagree. doctor.rs stale_records (453-456) defaults a missing `classification` to "tactical" then calls rule.is_stale; status.rs (120-126) gates on explicitly known classifications (the sprint-8 parity fix). Same crafted store: reference `doctor --json` -> "1 stale record(s) found"; OURS -> "2"; our status matches the reference. Cosmetic on disk (both --fix runs empty the file) but the report count, details and check status diverge. Solution: deepen StaleRule into the staleness module — `classify(&Value) -> Stale::Fresh | Stale{..} | NotClassified`; status and doctor both ask it, no defaulting at call sites; one table test (explicit/absent/unknown classification).

title: JS-quirk helpers smeared over three modules — one jsval seam for value_text/truthy/js_length/integer-key order/Math.round
description:
Architecture gate @ sprint 9, candidate 5 (Worth exploring). The sprint-8 rewrite did NOT quarantine the JS emulation: records.rs holds value_text; commands/outcome.rs keeps truthy (x15), js_length (x8), value_text (x14) private; commands/status.rs re-implements JS string coercion in Counter on top of lib value_text plus f64_to_u64 and json_num (x10). Each new parity slice re-derives the same quirks; the "undefined"/NaN/integer-key rules are pinned only by per-module unit tests. Solution: a jsval module (integer-key enumeration, value_text, truthy, js_length, Math.round) with command modules choosing surfaces (output.rs keeps rendering). Benefits: one test surface for JS quirks, reuse for the next parity slices.

GATE @ SPRINT 12 — unchanged validity: value_text lives in lib records.rs:144; outcome.rs keeps truthy (11 calls), js_length (7), value_text (14) private; status.rs Counter + f64_to_u64 + json_num re-implement undefined/NaN/integer-key-order on top. One lib jsval seam, one quirk test surface.

title: unknown-type surfaces: validate text and doctor status diverge from the reference
description: Sprint-10 spec-review finding (2026-10-04, ml 0.10.7), out of scope for mulch-5f8a but real. A store line with a present-but-unregistered type (e.g. "zzzcustom"): reference `validate` exits 1 with `Unknown record type "zzzcustom" (id=...) ...` (the register/remove/--allow-unknown-types hint text) AND reference `doctor` reports schema-validation as PASS; ours prints the shorter ``Unknown record `zzzcustom` `` and doctor reports FAIL. Two surfaces to reconcile (validate message + doctor check status) plus the --allow-unknown-types interaction.

title: delete: argument-order — reference checks the domain before the id/mode exclusivity
description: Sprint-12 spec-review finding (2026-10-04, pre-existing, not a regression): `mulch delete x` (no id) — ours fails the id/mode check first ("Error: must provide a record ID, --records, or --all-except."), the reference reports the unknown domain first ("Error: domain \"x\" not found in config.\nAvailable domains: d"). Reorder the checks in delete::run (domain lookup before the mode/id validation) and pin both orders differentially. Informational sibling: the reference's future unknown-domain surfaces differ per command (query/rank/prime/search use capital-D + Hint with `ml add` wording; ready uses 'Available:' instead of 'Available domains:') — pin per-command when those commands land, do not normalize.

title: record batch: mixed-batch partial writes (reference writes the valid records, reports the invalid ones)
description: Split from mulch-b8ca (sprint 14 delivered the validation model — structured SubErrors, additionalProperties, property types/enums/patterns). REMAINING: the mixed-batch write interplay. Reference (record.ts processStdinRecords + the batch caller): records that pass validation are WRITTEN even when others fail; the error entries list only the failures; created/updated reflect the writes and the json envelope's success is `errors.length === 0 || created + updated > 0` (probe 2026-10-04: batch [valid named dup, invalid id] -> created 0, updated 1, errors [Record 1: ...], rc 1). OURS is all-or-nothing (any error -> nothing written, created 0, rc 1) — deliberate since sprint 2, now known divergent. Also in scope: the nested subschema errors beyond the object/array type check (outcomes items: status enum, duration number, additionalProperties inside outcome/evidence objects) with their ajv paths.
